newsitem.title: USA: Man rescued after 36 hours floating near Maine.
newsitem.headline: Man rescued after 36 hours floating near Maine.

text.p: Mark McKenney figured he had two choices as his inflatable raft floated from shore -- grab hold of a nearby lobster buoy or end up in Europe.
He escaped with only minor injuries after spending 36 hours trapped four miles offshore in bitter cold, pounded by 12-foot waves that threatened to swamp his small craft.

The East Boothbay man's ordeal began Sunday afternoon when the outboard motor on his 14-foot inflatable raft failed. The wind and waves pushed him to open sea until he managed to grab a buoy anchored to a string of lobster traps.
"If I hadn't grabbed that my next stop would have been Spain or Portugal," McKenney, 31, told the Portland Press Herald.
Trapped without food, water, a life jacket or other emergency equipment, he was found by a fishing boat Tuesday morning. He was treated for hypothermia and dehydration.
